Resolves #21254

The spec-retirement guard now asks a commit for a `spec-retired:` account only when its range lands the deletion: the unit spec, followed back through the range's earlier renames, is in the tree of the range's merge base, and neither it nor that base path is in the tree of its tip. A spec the branch added and deletes again, or one a later commit restores at its path, no longer reads as retired, while a real deletion is still reported. `landedDeletions(range, git, shas)` reads the two trees and the range's renames once per range, only after a commit of the range deletes a spec, and fails closed like the commit-tree read.

Evidence: L2 (unit arms, one against a real git repository, red on `dev`; the old and the new guard run against #21154's merge ref) → L2 required (every AC is unit-level).

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1: a spec the range's merge base does not hold yields no violation | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkSpecRetirement.spec.mjs`, "only a deletion the whole range lands needs an account (#21254)", first case |
| AC-2: a base spec that a later commit restores yields no violation | CI-covered: the same arm, second case |
| AC-3: a base spec deleted for good is still reported, also after a rename in the range; existing arms stay green | CI-covered: the same arm's control case, and "a base spec renamed and then deleted still needs an account (#21256 review)" (real git); the 61 existing arms run on the extended port |
| AC-4: the #21154 shape in a real fixture repository, red on `dev` | CI-covered: "a spec the branch adds, deletes and renames a new version onto needs no account (#21254)" |
| AC-5: an unresolvable merge base or an unreadable tree throws | CI-covered: "an unreadable base or tip tree REFUSES too, and so does an unresolvable merge base (#21254)" |

## Deltas from ticket
- The merge base comes from the range itself rather than from `origin/dev` (recorded in the ticket's The Fix). CI's `origin/dev..HEAD` gets the same answer, and the guard's fixture repositories, which have no `origin/dev`, keep working.
- The spec's port fake gains `mergeBase` and a base tree that holds the deleted spec, so the existing arms keep their meaning. The ENOBUFS arm now fails the commit's own tree read; the new AC-5 arm covers the base and tip reads.

## Test Evidence
- Red-first on `dev` `a5e102c8f6`, with this branch's spec and the guard untouched: 3 of 64 failed, exactly the new arms. Both no-loss shapes came back as violations, and the base and tip reads never ran.
- Against #21154's merge ref (`origin/dev..refs/pull/21154/merge`): the guard on `dev` reports `4df6805e49 test/playwright/unit/examples/ConfigurationViewport.spec.mjs`, and this branch's guard reports nothing.
- Review round 1, the rename-then-delete history: the new real-git arm fails on `907e5115c9` (1 of 65) and passes at `74b737b1b1` (66 of 66). At that head the guard still reports nothing on `origin/dev..refs/remotes/pr/21154`.
